threat_assessment:
They see five colours, a tutor on a stick and four pregame Game Changers, and file you archenemy before you untap. Let them — wrong object. Sisay lands turn three in 95 games of 100: that is your floor. Play the two turns after her.

Alone she is a 2/2 and the gate reads cheaper than two: three legal cards, one adding no colour, no legendary lands. Never fire into a cold board. Your legends' colours set the ceiling, not mana: 10 targets at one, 23 at two, 28 at three, 33 at four, nothing at five — nothing here costs over five. Buy colour two cheap, stop at four, hold protection.

Five cards carry {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}: Sisay's and Najeela's activations, Jodah and Esika spend it; only Jegantha adds it, and at five she is legal only at power six, four colours already out, so you can pay anyway. Fix mana early; she is payoff, not fix. Black is the real gate — 21 sources against 36, on curve 61% against white's 94% and green's 95%. Take black off every fetch, and lay the second before the greedy one.

Four things flip you archenemy: five untapped sources covering all five colours beside an untapped Sisay; a bill-payer (Jegantha, Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Esika); Najeela; two activations in one cycle.

So sequence colours onto bodies nobody fears — Katilda, Kinnan, Lotho, Kambal, Kutzil, Saffi, two mana for two rungs each. Leave Najeela and Jodah in the library. Never bluff open mana either; your interaction is all unfetchable. Tap out behind a modest permanent and look poor. Sit a turn on Rhystic Study too: a non-legendary Game Changer paints you faster than she can.

Good pilots kill the rung, not Sisay, and your fetch shrinks. Audit single-sourced colours every turn; take Shalai the moment she is legal.

Embrace it on stack 002. Najeela with Derevi is an unbounded combat loop: five colours untapped before first combat, both creatures alive, damage through to a player. It grows its own board, and combat two breaks even, five untaps against five mana. Pay through Command Tower and Plaza of Heroes' any-colour mode for no life, leave City of Brass and Mana Confluence untapped, count blockers — Derevi must connect. It re-buys Sisay's pips, so the turn you present her you stop fetching.

Take the seat on purpose, on your turn: three colours down, five pips payable, protection or Kutzil up.

One thing stays open: whether a legend you just fetched helps pay that turn's next activation. The resolution that asked failed its check — plan on one activation per cycle.
matchups:
Sweeper control. A wrath is near certain across four seats and takes board and ladder both, 28 targets to 3: keep a two-colour legend in hand. Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention and Boros Charm's indestructible mode cover destruction only, never exile or a -X/-X like your own Toxic Deluge. Protection arrives turn two on average, by six in 80 of 100 games: fetch into it. Wipe with Deluge yourself, worst threat first; you rebuild cheapest here, plus two mana per command-zone trip.

Stax and tax. You are the beatdown: race the lock. Five coloured pips, no generic, every turn: the most tax-exposed shape going. Recount activations under the tax, not cards. Three accelerants fail a coloured activation: Delighted Halfling (legendary spells), Unclaimed Territory (creature spells), Sol Ring (colourless). Two pay anyway: Plaza of Heroes' any-colour-among-legendary mode, and Secluded Courtyard's "or activate an ability" — name Human. Katilda taps Human creatures for mana, making Sisay a white source. Fetch the piece locking YOU: Loran, three mana from colour two, eats an artifact or enchantment, Teferi's minus behind.

Aggro. You are 120 life behind across three defences, four bodies on turn six. Stop racing; buy virtual answers. Thalia (their lands and creatures tapped), Sheoldred (two life a draw), Shalai (hexproof) and Flowering (ward) each blank plans at three seats: legendary, two to four mana, one activation from colour two. If one seat races you, make it a subgame: spend the minimum, watch the others. You answer creatures, artifacts and enchantments, never graveyards or lands: tax those.

Combo. Invert: hold pips for interaction, count their open mana, stop climbing. Spend your one Path to Exile the turn the piece lands. The rest is what Sisay cannot see: six counterspells, Fierce Guardianship, Flawless Maneuver, Drannith Magistrate and Grand Abolisher, all in the 26 unfetchable cards. Mulligan for enablers and disruption, never payoffs; take Teferi (sorcery speed) or Kutzil (spells off on your turn) over Najeela while combo lives.

Fair value midrange. You are the control seat: slow down, look boring after each fetch, sequence Najeela and Jodah last.

Graveyard hate. Mostly a blank: a Bojuka Bog aimed here, not at the reanimator seat, is free. Say nothing. Do not build on your own yard: Saffi's trigger is the whole recursion suite. Keep Dauthi Voidwalker for those decks; he arrives by draw.

Never keep a hand for the nine combo lines nobody has resolved.

cover.tagline: The tutor that widens every time it fires - and the five-pip bill that comes due every time.
cover.identity: Sisay, Weatherlight Captain is a repeatable battlefield tutor whose reach is bought in colours: she is a 2/2 plus one for each colour among your other legendary permanents, and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} searches out any legendary permanent with mana value strictly less than her power. That makes this an access curve rather than a card curve - 3 legal targets at power 2, then 10, 23, 28 and 33 as the board picks up colours - funded by 40 lands and a small battery of bodies that can produce five distinct coloured pips at once. It is a bracket 4 (Optimized) list on contents alone: four Game Changers put the floor there independently of any combo line, and the Najeela combat loop is the closer.

how_it_wins:
Five colours, a tutor commander, forty lands: the table files you as a greedy pile. Let them. She is a {2}{W} creature with no tap symbol and no once-per-turn clause; this deck's currency is access.

Read her power, never her cost: a 2/2 plus one per colour among your OTHER legendary permanents, fetching any legend cheaper than that. Zero colours, three legal targets; one, ten; two, twenty-three; four, all 33 — nothing costs more than five. The rung that matters is one to two: +13 targets, Najeela legal. Colour-dense legend first, then activate. Stop at four; the fifth buys stats, not access.

Then the bill: four cards demand {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} and only Jegantha adds it. Sol Ring is colourless, Delighted Halfling legendary spells only, Unclaimed Territory creature spells only — deploy her early off those three, then pay with the six that can: Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha, Esika, Relic of Legends, Selvala.

Stop mulliganing for the captain: turn three in 8,028 of 10,000 seeded games, turn six in 99 of 100. The gate is Sisay plus a multi-colour mana body: a little over half by six. Keep the fuel.

Removal is a shopping list, not a card in hand: one unconditional creature answer, one sweeper. The rest is tax, legendary, mana value 2 to 4: Thalia (creatures and nonbasics enter tapped), Teferi and Kutzil (turns), Kambal and Sheoldred (spells and draws). Fetch the tax that hurts the seat beating you.

Close with Najeela. She and Derevi are the one line cleared against the Comprehensive Rules — an unbounded combat loop, no life cost. It re-buys five colours a combat and wants five creatures connecting; present it when the base pays that toll.

Know the hole. Twenty-six nonland cards are not legendary, so she never sees them: three of the six that pay her, every counterspell, both free protection spells, all four Game Changers. She finds payoffs; you draw fuel.

card_roles.Sisay, Weatherlight Captain: Count colours before you count mana: she is 2/2 plus one for every colour among your other legendary permanents, and she finds any legendary permanent cheaper than that power. No tap symbol and no once-per-turn line, so the only ceiling on her is how often you can raise {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}.
card_roles.An Offer You Can't Refuse: One blue mana to stop the wrath or the exile aimed at your ladder. The two Treasures you hand back cost less than rebuilding four rungs — spend it on the spell that takes your board, not the one that annoys you.
card_roles.Arcane Denial: Two mana to keep an activation alive, and you replace the card on the next upkeep. Point it at whatever would cost you the most colours.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Any colour in the identity for two mana, which makes it one of the few rocks that pays a real pip of her bill. Play it ahead of a three-drop, never after.
card_roles.Birds of Paradise: A one-mana source of any colour, which is the best turn-one card a deck needing five different colours can have. Treat it as a land and protect it like one.
card_roles.Bloom Tender: One mana for each colour among your permanents, so it scales with the ladder you are already climbing. Four colours on board and it pays four of her five pips by itself.
card_roles.Boros Charm: Indestructible for every permanent you control is the mode you keep it for; the four damage is a footnote. Hold it the moment a red or black seat is one card away from a sweeper.
card_roles.Bristly Bill, Spine Sower: A green rung for two mana that turns each land drop into a counter. Fetch him early because green is missing, not late because the pump is nice.
card_roles.Dauthi Voidwalker: Double black on turn two is why black carries the highest source target in the deck — cast him on curve when you can, and let the exile clause shut a graveyard seat off. Not legendary, so she will never hand him to you.
card_roles.Delighted Halfling: Deploy her a turn early and uncounterable, then stop counting it: the coloured mana is for legendary spells only and buys none of her activation. Excellent first drop, false friend from turn three onward.
card_roles.Derevi, Empyrial Tactician: Three rungs on one three-mana body, the biggest single climb in the deck, plus an untap trigger every time one of your creatures connects. He is also the quiet half of the kill — never trade him off casually.
card_roles.Dihada, Binder of Wills: Three rungs and a four-card dig for legends with Treasures attached. Remember the +2 as a protection button: vigilance, lifelink and indestructible on the captain until your next turn.
card_roles.Dispel: One mana for the instant that would blow you out mid-activation. Keep it up against the combo seat and ship it from any opener that has one land.
card_roles.Drannith Magistrate: Shuts off every command zone, graveyard and exile cast at the table at once. You have to draw him — she cannot see a nonlegendary body.
card_roles.Emiel the Blessed: Three mana a blink, so spend it on the enter-the-battlefield value you actually need, or to save a mana dork from a removal spell. The loops he appears in have no passing stack; play the value, not the promise.
card_roles.Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic: One mana of any colour, and she grants that same ability to every other legendary creature you control — the board you fetched becomes fuel for the next fetch. On the battlefield she is green only, so count one rung, not five.
card_roles.Esper Sentinel: A white one-drop that taxes their first noncreature spell every turn, and the ladder pumps the tax as it grows. Cast it turn one and forget about it.
card_roles.Faeburrow Elder: One mana per colour among your permanents, and it grows with them. Both Vivid dorks are cards she cannot fetch, so if you want them you draw them.
card_roles.Fellwar Stone: Two mana for whatever colours the table's lands can produce, which in a four-player pod is usually the colour you are short. Expect less from it against a mono-colour seat.
card_roles.Fierce Guardianship: Free while you control a commander, so hold it on the turn you tap out to climb. It is the answer to the removal spell pointed at her and to the counterspell pointed at your fetch.
card_roles.Flawless Maneuver: Free indestructible for your whole board on the turn a sweeper resolves — the cheapest way to keep four rungs instead of restarting from three legal targets.
card_roles.Flowering of the White Tree: Ward {1} on every legend you control makes cheap removal miss the captain, and the +2/+1 is another point of her power. At two mana it is the cheapest insurance she can fetch for herself.
card_roles.Grand Abolisher: During your turn they cannot cast spells or activate their artifacts, creatures and enchantments. That is the window you climb three rungs in — but you have to draw him.
card_roles.Heliod, Sun-Crowned: An indestructible white rung that hands out lifelink for two mana and turns every life gain into a counter. Legal to fetch at power 4.
card_roles.Heroic Intervention: Two mana, hexproof and indestructible for everything you own. It beats a targeted-removal turn and a wrath with the same card, so hold it rather than jam it.
card_roles.Ioreth of the Healing House: Untaps two other legendary creatures, which here means two more taps out of the pip battery. Fetch her once the mana bodies are already down, not before.
card_roles.Jegantha, the Wellspring: The only card in the deck that adds all five colours off a single tap — and at mana value 5 she is legal to fetch only once four colours are already out. Treat her as the payoff, never as the fix.
card_roles.Jodah, the Unifier: Five distinct pips to cast, the biggest anthem in the deck, and a free legendary spell every time you cast one from hand. He is the ceiling target: power 6 or nothing.
card_roles.Kambal, Consul of Allocation: Two rungs at three mana and a bill on every noncreature spell the table casts. Against a spell-heavy seat he is your removal suite.
card_roles.Katilda, Dawnhart Prime: Two rungs for two mana, and every Human you control taps for mana — the captain included. One of the best turn-two plays in the deck.
card_roles.Kenrith, the Returned King: Five modes on one white body, so fetch him when you already have mana and need whichever thing the board is missing. Reachable only at power 6.
card_roles.Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy: Two rungs for two mana, and every nonland permanent you tap for mana produces one extra — a whole additional pip out of Bloom Tender or Jegantha.
card_roles.Kodama of the West Tree: A green rung whose modified creatures fetch you a basic land on damage, with trample attached. It matters more than it reads in a deck that makes counters.
card_roles.Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar: Two rungs at three mana, and your opponents cannot cast spells during your turn. Buy that window before you present the kill, not after.
card_roles.Loran of the Third Path: Your only fetchable answer to an artifact or an enchantment, and she draws you a card every turn afterward. Go and get her the moment a lock piece lands.
card_roles.Lotho, Corrupt Shirriff: Two rungs for two mana, and every second spell any player casts hands you a Treasure. That Treasure pays a real coloured pip, which most of your acceleration does not.
card_roles.Mikaeus, the Lunarch: One of only three cards legal at her base power, and the one that grows the rest of the board. Cast him with X when you can — whether a fetched copy survives with no X chosen is an open question on the record.
card_roles.Mox Amber: Free, legal at her base power, and it makes a colour only if a legendary creature or planeswalker is already out. It is the cold-start fetch that adds no rung by itself, so play a legend first.
card_roles.Najeela, the Blade-Blossom: Your red rung at three mana and half of the verified kill. Fetch her on the turn you can pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} in combat with five creatures able to connect — any earlier and you have simply told the table whom to kill.
card_roles.Negate: Two mana for the wrath, the lock piece or the removal aimed at your commander. Not legendary, so it arrives by draw and never by fetch.
card_roles.Path to Exile: One mana, exile, instant speed — the only unconditional creature answer in the deck. Spend it on the creature that ends the game, not the one that is merely large.
card_roles.Raff Capashen, Ship's Mage: Two rungs, and every legendary spell you own gains flash. Deploy the ladder on their end step, then untap with the mana up for her activation.
card_roles.Reki, the History of Kamigawa: A green rung that draws a card for every legendary spell you cast — the closest thing to a draw engine she can fetch for you.
card_roles.Relic of Legends: Any colour, and it taps your untapped legendary creatures for more of the same. One of the six pieces that genuinely pays her bill, and one of the three of those you have to draw.
card_roles.Rhystic Study: They pay or you draw, and this deck's card advantage sits at 7 against a budget of 10 — so resolve it as early as the mana allows. She will never find it for you.
card_roles.Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolari: A blue rung at two mana that untaps whenever you cast a legendary spell, with looting attached. She is blue only on the front face — count one rung, not two.
card_roles.Saffi Eriksdotter: Two rungs for two mana and a sacrifice that returns a dying creature. Hold her over whichever body is currently paying your pips.
card_roles.Samut, Voice of Dissent: Flash, haste for the team, and a {W} untap every turn. She is legal only at power 6, so she tends to be the last rung rather than a step toward it.
card_roles.Seedborn Muse: Untaps everything during every opponent's untap step — three extra activation windows per turn cycle at a four-player table. Not legendary, so you draw her or you play without her.
card_roles.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: X mana in any combination of colours for the greatest power among your creatures, which is frequently the captain herself. The fetchable half of the pip battery, legal at power 4.
card_roles.Shalai, Voice of Plenty: Hexproof for you and every other creature you control, on a body she can fetch at power 5. This is the answer to a targeted-removal seat that you can go and get.
card_roles.Sheoldred, the Apocalypse: A rung in your scarcest colour at four mana, plus two life off every card an opponent draws. Fetch her against the seat whose plan is drawing cards.
card_roles.Silence: One mana buys their entire turn. Save it for the turn you present the loop rather than spending it on a wrath you could have taken.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Two colourless on turn one, which deploys the captain a turn early and pays nothing toward her activation. Take the speed — then remember it made no colour.
card_roles.Surrak Dragonclaw: Three rungs on one body, flash, and your creature spells cannot be countered. A late rung at power 6, and the one that beats a blue seat.
card_roles.Swan Song: One mana against a wrath, a counterspell or a combo instant. The 2/2 Bird they get is cheap next to the turn you would have spent rebuilding.
card_roles.Teferi, Time Raveler: Two rungs on a planeswalker, and while he lives the table may only act at sorcery speed — that is an activation window with no counterspell in it. His −3 bounces an artifact, creature or enchantment and replaces itself.
card_roles.Thalia, Heretic Cathar: A white rung that makes their creatures and nonbasic lands enter tapped — a turn of tempo taken from three seats with one card. One of the first taxes to go and fetch.
card_roles.Toxic Deluge: Your only sweeper, and you choose both X and the turn. You rebuild from a wipe cheaper than the rest of the table does, so do not hold it waiting for perfect.
card_roles.Yoshimaru, Ever Faithful: A white rung for one mana that grows with every legendary permanent that follows it. Legal at her base power, which makes him a live fetch on the cold-start turn.

mulligan:
Everyone mulligans hunting for the commander. She is the one card you do not need — turn-three Sisay in 8,028 games of 10,000. Keep for what she cannot go and get.

Six cards in the 99 pay her five-pip activation; three are not legendary, so those three only arrive off the top. Fuel and colours in the opener, payoffs later from the battlefield.

A keep is three things. Two to four lands with one that makes any colour — Command Tower, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Exotic Orchard, Forbidden Orchard, any fetch, Secluded Courtyard named on Human. An accelerant that pays a coloured pip: Birds of Paradise, Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, Relic of Legends. And a cheap multicolour legend, the piece that turns casting her into climbing.

Katilda, Kinnan, Lotho and Saffi buy two rungs for two mana, Derevi three for three. A seven with one of those and an any-colour source is a snap keep.

Ship the payoff hand on sight. Jodah, Kenrith, Surrak and Samut over two lands is four uncastable cards in front of a 2/2 whose menu is Mox Amber, Mikaeus and Yoshimaru — she could have fetched all three.

Ship the fast hand that pays nothing. Sol Ring plus Delighted Halfling deploys her a turn early and covers not one pip of what she does next — your best-looking opener until you tap out.

Ship counterspells on one land. Protection is there by turn six in 80 games of 100; you are not the hand holding the answer on turn one.

Two habits. An early accelerant arrives by turn six in only 64 games of 100, so a seven holding one is ahead of your curve. And count colours, not lands: you keep 84.2% of first sevens on the land rule alone, so lands were never the question.
upgrades:
Five cards in the 99 carry {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}; four spend it, and only Jegantha adds it. One activation a turn — and six of these ten buy a second. The ladder runs 3 / 10 / 23 / 28 / 33 targets, and the rung is one colour to two: +13, the first mana-value-3 legend.

The six fail in two ways. Intruder Alarm, Freed from the Real and Marvin, Murderous Mimic untap a body you already control — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Relic of Legends, Jegantha — so they need a board. Cryptolith Rite, Chromatic Lantern and Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth change what your permanents produce, good on an empty table.

Three are fetchable, not drawn: Marvin at 2, Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose at 3, Urborg at 0 and legal at base power, where the menu is three cards — zero legendary lands in the deck.

Black is thin: 21 sources against a 36 yardstick where every other colour is asked 22, only 12 of them lands. Urborg and Chromatic Lantern change what the 40 land copies are instead of adding a pip. Neither moves the colour-sources axis: the maths counts sources per card and models no static grant. The instrument, not a verdict.

Stack 002 re-buys {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} every combat; the deck affords it about once. Bear Umbra alone aims at the toll, not the first payment: its untap rides an attack trigger, before the bill. Two other cards hold the same record; one slot.

Two picks move a counted axis: Beast Within, interaction-breadth 3 classes to 4 and land 0 to 1 — the class nothing in the 99 answers; Vito, threat-density 3 to 4. Adoption runs EDHREC 25 to 1,720, bracket flat at 4 on all ten.

Nothing here is verified, nor are the ten combo lines already inside the deck, four of them two-card infinites. The obsolescence index is no help either. Over two Vivid dorks it proposes ten replacements at 0.942 to 0.9755, listing cost, power, toughness, flying — never mana; and Sol Ring over Fellwar Stone at 0.9746, a coloured source for two colourless. It measures similarity; this deck buys colours.
mana_base:
Forty land copies across thirty-nine entries, seventeen with a tapped clause — 42% against a one-in-three budget. The figure underneath is better: zero enter tapped unconditionally. Nine are shocks, tapped only if you decline two life. The other eight read "unless you have two or more opponents", which at a four-player table is not a tapped land at all.

Pip share and source share disagree here on purpose. White carries 38.3% of the pips on 23.1% of the sources; red 8.0% on 18.5%. Elsewhere that gap is a misallocation. Here the cost that runs the deck asks one of every colour, so the base is levelled rather than tuned — 27 green, 26 white, 22 blue, 21 black, 21 red, a spread of six across the rainbow.

Black is the exception and carries its own target: 36 sources against 22 for the other four. It is the colour whose cards want two pips — Dauthi Voidwalker on turn two, Sheoldred at four — so the target sizes for two black sources by turn three. Twelve black lands gets there on curve 29.9% of the time. Every other colour lands between 70.4% and 78.7% on lands alone.

Nine dorks and five rocks close that gap. Counted in, black rises to 21 sources and 61.0%, and the rest go to 89.5% red, 90.7% blue, 94.4% white, 95.1% green. That is why 17 ramp pieces against a 10-12 budget reads as fixing rather than speed: Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder are load-bearing lands with legs.

One accounting rule decides more here than anywhere else. "Spend this mana only" counts for nothing unless the clause reaches abilities, so Delighted Halfling and Unclaimed Territory are zeroed, while Plaza of Heroes keeps an unrestricted coloured mode and Secluded Courtyard says "or activate an ability". Raw mana crosses five on turn six at a mean of 5.869, against 3.187 on turn three. From six on, the question is not how much but which.

combo_lines.002:
The clause is CR 508.4: a creature put onto the battlefield attacking "never 'attacked'" for triggers. Najeela's tokens are invisible to the trigger that made them, so the loop grows between combats, never inside one.

CR 603.2c gives Derevi one untap trigger per creature that connects, not one per damage event; the activation stays five. Attackers follow 2A - 1: three, five, nine, seventeen, thirty-three — combat 1 two short and funded from outside, 2 exact, 3 four to spare.

On life the popular telling is wrong: mana abilities are not mandatory (CR 118.3c) and Command Tower with Plaza of Heroes cover all five colours, so nothing compels a tap of City of Brass or Mana Confluence. Zero life a combat.

CR 506.4 lists removal from combat exhaustively; a player leaving the game is not among the causes, so the seventeen attackers stay.

The holding: real, deterministic, unbounded — and not a two-card infinite, since neither makes mana. Five creatures connecting and a base paying {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} each combat are requirements. On the deck's nine other combo records, the record is silent.

editors_letter:
Most commanders cost mana and hand you a body. This one costs mana and hands you a shopping licence.

Sisay is a 2/2 who grows by one for every colour among the other legendary permanents you control, and her ability goes and gets a legendary permanent cheaper than she is strong. So the currency this deck runs on is not cards and it is not mana. It is access — how much of your own library you are allowed to reach right now — and every other card in the 99 is either widening that number or spending it. A two-mana legend in two colours is worth more here than a mana rock, and the reason is printed on the commander rather than on the card in your hand.

Two things make this one unusual and both belong at the top. The first is the bill: her ability costs five different coloured pips with no generic in it at all, so a good deal of the acceleration in this deck cannot pay for the thing the deck is about. Ledger has what that does to a turn-four board. The second is how little of it is settled. One resolution survived the checker, and Vera spends most of the Pilot's Log marking which claims are readings rather than rulings — including one of the Coach's, which he takes well.

Play this if you enjoy a deck that plays like a search problem, where you are not drawing answers so much as buying the right to go and fetch them, and where the price of the next one falls every time you pay. Play something else if you want a commander who ends games by attacking.

pilots_log.text:
Nobody says this at a five-colour table, so I will. You need five colours of mana — she does not turn on without them. You do not need five colours of legends, and chasing the fifth one is how you waste a turn.

Two colours among your other legendary permanents and her search opens to twenty-three of the thirty-three legends in this deck. That is the turn Najeela becomes a legal find. Four colours opens all thirty-three. The fifth adds a body to your board and not one card to her list. So the hand you keep is the one with a two-mana legend that brings two colours by itself — Kinnan, Katilda, Lotho, Saffi — and the fifth colour is the one you stop paying for.

The Coach's arithmetic I will sign. The climb he is imagining underneath it I cannot.

The countable part anyone can count. Sisay reads '+1/+1 for each color among other legendary permanents you control', and her ability finds 'a legendary permanent card with mana value less than Sisay's power' — less, not less than or equal. Set that against this 99, which holds thirty-three other legendary permanents and nothing above mana value five, and the ladder is 3, 10, 23, 28, 33 at nought through four colours, then 33 again at five. Power six buys everything. Power seven buys the same everything.

The activation itself is not on the record. Stack 001 walked exactly that escalation and the artifact fails; its own checker note says answers (a) through (e) were verified correct and the iteration bound ran out on one -X/-X clause under CR 613.4c. A note is not a verdict. Eight of this engine's eleven lines are drawn dashed, and every arrow leaving the dial is one of them.

Holding: you may count the ladder. Nobody has yet proved the climb.

Prices on the half that has been measured, and a gap where the other half should be.

The commander is not the scarce piece. Ten thousand seeded runs: Sisay is cast on a mean turn of 2.963, median three, and she is down by turn six in 99.1% of them. She starts every game in the command zone; nothing has to go right for you to have her.

The Coach's second colour carries no rate, because it was never declared as a target. Four are. Commander protection available: 88.4% assembled, 79.8% by turn six, mean turn 2.3. Early accelerant drawn: 74.7%, 63.8%, mean 2.836. Sisay online with a multi-colour mana engine: 67.9%, 55.8%, mean 4.219. Sisay online with a three-colour legend: 52.5%, 41.9%, mean 4.395, and that group is four cards.

The class he just built his opening hand around is not among them, and neither is a win line. I can tell you how often you hold protection. I cannot tell you how often you have two colours by turn three.

Take it. Ledger has no number for me and Vera will not let me call it proved, and I am not going to argue with either of them at a table where somebody has read the same file.

Here is what I do anyway, and it needs no ruling. I mulligan on colours, not on lands. Seven cards with five lands and Yoshimaru in them is a hand that casts her on three and hands her a list of ten. Seven cards with three lands and Kinnan in them casts her on three and hands her a list of twenty-three — and one of the twenty-three ends the game.

And I am dropping Rona from my list of two-colour twos. Vera is about to be right about that and I have made the mistake with the card in my hand.

She is, and it is the small one: Rona's card is blue and black, her front face is blue alone, and the dial reads the permanent, not the card. One colour until she transforms. Esika is the same trap facing the other way — a five-colour card standing on the battlefield green.

But since the Coach has moved to counting mana, read the cost out loud. The activation is {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}: five coloured pips, no generic symbol anywhere in it. That one fact disqualifies more of this deck's acceleration than any rules question could. Sol Ring adds {C}, and there is no generic for {C} to pay, so Sol Ring contributes nothing to the ability on any board. Delighted Halfling's coloured mode says 'Spend this mana only to cast a legendary spell', and an activated ability is not a spell — no rule number needed there, only the word.

Read the clause and not the phrase, though. Secluded Courtyard says 'or activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type', and Sisay is a Human Soldier, so named on Human it pays her fine.

Holding: two of your accelerants accelerate toward your commander without accelerating what she does.

What that bill costs in turns. Mean available mana is 3.187 at turn three, 4.063 at four, 4.894 at five, 5.869 at six. The activation is five, so on the average board the first payment lands between turns five and six — before anyone asks the five mana to be five different colours.

Sources: G 27, W 26, U 22, R 21, B 21. On-curve probability with rocks and dorks counted is 0.951 green, 0.944 white, 0.610 black; on lands alone black is 0.299. Black carries 11.1% of the pip load and 18.5% of the sources.

Seventeen of the forty land copies enter tapped. The land drop is made in 84.2% of runs at turn four and 63.7% at turn six.

So here is your turn-four habit, and it is a physical one. Before you tap anything, find your black source and put a finger on it.

Black is the pip that is not there. Command Tower, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Exotic Orchard, Forbidden Orchard — those five are your black, and they are also your white, your blue and your red. Behind them it thins out fast: the Swamp, Godless Shrine, Overgrown Tomb, Watery Grave, Luxury Suite. Marsh Flats, Polluted Delta and Verdant Catacombs can go and get one. Arid Mesa cannot.

The way you lose the activation is not drawing no black. It is having black and spending it on a two-drop. Tap the narrow land first, every time, and keep the five-colour ones for her.

On how much of this deck is proved, since it keeps coming up. One stack artifact carries a passing verdict. Twenty-one verified pairings come out of it and all twenty-one come off the same board — seven cards: Najeela, Derevi, Command Tower, Plaza of Heroes, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Exotic Orchard. No card in this deck appears in two passing stacks, so the load-bearing count is zero.

Against that, ten combo lines are fully contained in the 99 and four of them are two-card infinites. One of the ten is the pairing that stack settles. The other nine are records rather than findings.

The synergy graph has two edges falling inside this deck across the eighty-six of its cards it knows about. That is a measurement of the graph, not of the deck.

Then let me state the one thing here that is a holding rather than a reading. Stack 002 asked whether Najeela plus Derevi is a two-card infinite. It passed, and it answers no — and then answers something more useful.

Attackers follow A' = 2A − 1: three, five, nine, seventeen, thirty-three. Derevi's untap trigger fires per attacking creature, so the triggers scale while Najeela's cost stays fixed at five. Combat one is funded from the lands you had before combat, combat two is exactly break-even at five triggers against five mana, and from combat three the loop is in surplus. It is unbounded and it is not self-contained: it makes no mana of its own, it re-buys five distinct pips every combat, and it wants five of your creatures connecting with a player.

The floor line costs zero life, because Command Tower covers the black and Plaza of Heroes covers the other four — tapped, untapped by a trigger and retapped inside one combat damage step, three times over.

Holding: an unbounded engine with a bill attached, not a combo.

And that is the part I can hand you as a count. Damage goes six, eight, twelve, twenty, thirty-six. The first opponent is dead during combat four. The second is gone by combat six. You do not need this to be infinite. You need it to reach four.

So do not start it because it is available. Start it when five bodies can get through and the five pips are on the table rather than in the plan.

And take the zero-life floor seriously. If you are tapping City of Brass and Mana Confluence to run this, you are paying life for a line that never asked for it. Tap the Tower and the Plaza.

One more thing about the Plaza, and it is the sharpest item in the file.

That stack taps it for four of the five pips through its third mode, '{T}: Add one mana of any color among legendary permanents you control'. The mana analysis credits Plaza with zero colour sources. Both are correct: the measurement counts unconditional mana and both of Plaza's coloured modes are conditional, while the stack shows a board where the condition is met. The model records the disagreement instead of picking a winner, which I think is the honest thing to do with it.

The part with teeth is the type line. Plaza is a Land. Sisay searches for a legendary permanent card, Plaza is not legendary, and no fetchland here finds it either — so the mode that hands a legendary creature hexproof and indestructible is protection this commander can never go and get.

It generalises. Twenty-six of the ninety-nine are nonland and not legendary, and that set holds every instant in the deck.

Holding: she cannot fetch her own insurance.

The insurance measures well regardless. Commander protection available is eleven cards: 57.4% in the opening seven, 67.0% by turn three, 79.8% by turn six, 88.4% assembled, mean turn 2.3. The group that moves her power by three at once is four cards, mean turn 4.395.

So the half Vera says the commander cannot reach is the half this deck holds earliest and most often, and the half she was built to reach arrives after turn four on average.

The number I still do not have is the last one. No declared target measures Najeela alongside a mana base that can make all five colours, so the only kill this deck has verified has never been priced. Whatever rate you are carrying for that is yours, not mine.

Then hold the two mana, and that is my close.

Everything in this deck is a rung and she is the ladder. Lose her and you pay two more the next time and you start again from a board with no colours on it. Nothing you fetch is worth the turn you spent tapped out to fetch it.

Two-colour legend on two. Her on three. Activate when you can pay all five and still say no to somebody. Count to four colours and stop counting. Count to four combats and swing.

And when the table tells you Sisay is just a mana sink, agree with them warmly and keep the Swan Song up.
